translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus by the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus our hope,
writing to Timothy, a true son in the faith: Grace, mercy, and peace to you from God our Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
As I urged you to remain in Ephesus when I was going to Macedonia, instruct certain people not to teach a different doctrine
and not to pay attention to myths and endless genealogies. These give rise to questions rather than God's plan, which is through faith.
The goal of what has been entrusted to us is love from a pure heart, a conscience, and faith without hypocrisy.
Some people have missed these things and turned aside to empty talk.
They want to be teachers of the law, but they do not understand what they are saying or what they are asserting so confidently.
But we know that the law is good if someone uses it properly,

knowing this: The law is not laid down for a righteous person, but for the lawless and disobedient, the ungodly and sinners, the defiled and profane, those who kill their fathers or mothers, and murderers,
for sexually immoral people, men who sleep with males, kidnappers, liars, those who swear falsely, and anything else that opposes sound teaching,
in keeping with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, which has been entrusted to me.
I thank Christ Jesus our Lord, who gives me strength, because he considered me faithful and appointed me to service,
although I was formerly a blasphemer, a persecutor, and an abusive person. But I was shown mercy because I did these things ignorantly, in unbelief.
And the grace of our Lord overflowed, along with faith and love in Christ Jesus.
This saying is trustworthy and deserves every honor: Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost.
But for this reason I was shown mercy: so that Christ Jesus might demonstrate all his patience in me first, making me an example for those who would believe in him for eternal life.
To the King of the ages, the immortal, invisible God, who alone is God, be honor and glory forever and ever. Amen.
I entrust this instruction to you, my son Timothy, in keeping with the prophecies concerning you, so that through them you may fight the good fight,
holding on to faith and a good conscience. Some have abandoned this conscience and suffered shipwreck in their faith.
Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that he might discipline them not to blaspheme.
Therefore, I urge you, before everything else, to make petitions, prayers, intercessions, and thanksgivings for everyone,
for kings and all who are in positions of authority, so that we may lead a quiet and peaceful life in all godliness and dignity.
This is good and acceptable before God our Savior,
who wants everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
For there is one God, and one mediator between God and human beings, the man Christ Jesus.
He gave himself as a ransom for everyone—the testimony given at its appointed times.
For this I was appointed a herald and an apostle—I am telling the truth; I am not lying—a teacher of the nations in faith and truth.
So I want men to pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands without anger or dispute.
Likewise, women should dress in orderly clothing, with modesty and good judgment, adorning themselves not with braided hair, gold, pearls, or expensive clothes,
but with what is fitting for women who say that they worship God: good deeds.
Let a woman learn quietly, in complete submission.
But I do not permit a woman to teach or to rule over her husband; instead, she should remain quiet.
For Adam was formed first, and Eve afterward.
And Adam was not deceived, but the woman was deceived and fell into transgression.
But she will be saved through bearing children, if they continue in faith, love, and holiness, with self-control.
This saying is trustworthy: whoever wants to be a bishop desires a good work.
A bishop, then, must be beyond reproach, married to one wife, sober, sensible, orderly, hospitable, and able to teach.
He must not be a drunkard or violent, but gentle, not quarrelsome or a lover of money.
He must manage his own household well, keeping his children in submission and in complete dignity.
But if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he take care of God's church?
He must not be a new convert, so that he does not become proud and fall under the devil's condemnation.
He must also have a good reputation among outsiders, so that he does not fall into disgrace and the devil's trap.
Likewise, deacons must be dignified, not speak with a double tongue, not drink much wine, and not be greedy for shameful gain.
They must hold to the mystery of the faith with a clean conscience.
Let them also be tested first; afterward, let them serve as deacons if there is no charge of wrongdoing against them.
Likewise, women must be dignified, not slanderers, sober, and faithful in everything.
Let deacons be married to one wife, managing their children and their households well.
For those who have served well as deacons gain a good standing for themselves and great confidence in the faith in Christ Jesus.
I am writing these things to you, hoping to come soon.
But if I am delayed, you will know how one should conduct oneself in God's household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and support of the truth.

And undeniably, great is the mystery of divinity: he appeared in the flesh, was vindicated in the Spirit, appeared to angels, was proclaimed among the nations, was believed in throughout the world, and was taken up in glory.
But the Spirit says explicitly that in the last times some will turn away from the faith, giving their attention to deceptive spirits and teachings of demons.
Through the hypocrisy of liars whose consciences are seared.
They forbid marriage and require people to abstain from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by believers and those who have come to know the truth.
For everything God created is good, and nothing is to be rejected when it is received with thanksgiving.
For they are made holy through the word of the living God and prayer.
If you lay these things before the brothers, you will be a good servant of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of the faith and the good teaching that you have followed.
Reject foolish old women's tales, and train yourself in godliness.
For physical training is useful for a short time, but godliness is useful at all times, since it holds the promise of life, both here and in the life to come.
The saying is trustworthy and deserves every honor.
For this reason we toil and suffer insults, because we have put our trust in the living God, who is the Savior of all people, especially believers.
Command and teach these things.
Do not let anyone despise your youth, but be an example to believers in speech, in deeds, in faith, and in purity.
Until I come, attend to reading, exhortation, and teaching.
Do not neglect the gift within you, which was given to you through prophecy and the laying on of the elders’ hands.
Practice these things; devote yourself to them, so that your progress may be evident to everyone.
Pay attention to yourself, and continue in these things, in the teaching. For by doing this, you will save yourself and those who listen to you.
Do not rebuke older men harshly, but appeal to them as fathers, and to younger men as brothers.
Treat older women as mothers, and younger women as sisters, with complete purity.
Honor widows who are truly widows.
But if a widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to serve their own household and repay their parents, for this is good and acceptable before God.
But the woman who is truly a widow and has been left alone puts her hope in God and continues in supplications and prayers night and day.
But the woman who lives in self-indulgence is dead while she is still alive.
Command these things, so that they may not be found at fault in anything.
But if anyone does not care for his own people, especially those of his household, he has denied the faith and is worse than an unbeliever.
Let a widow be enrolled only if she is at least sixty years old and has lived with only one husband.
She must have a reputation for good deeds: that she brought up her children, welcomed strangers, washed the feet of the holy ones, helped those in distress, and devoted herself to every good work.
But refuse younger widows, for when their desires lead them to rebel against Christ, they want to marry.
They bring judgment upon themselves because they have disregarded their first pledge of faith.
At the same time, they learn to be idle, going around from house to house. They are not only idle, but also gossips and busybodies, saying things they should not.
So I want young women to marry, bear children, and manage their households, giving the opponent no opportunity to speak evil of us.
For some have already turned aside to follow Satan.
If a believing woman has a widow in her care, let her provide for her, and do not let the church be burdened, so that it can provide for those who are truly widows.
Let the elders who lead well be given double honor, especially those who work hard at speaking and teaching.
For Scripture says, “You must not muzzle an ox while it is threshing,” and, “The worker deserves his wages.”
Do not accept an accusation against an elder unless it comes through two or three witnesses.
Rebuke those who sin in front of everyone, so that the rest will also be afraid.
I solemnly charge you before God and Christ Jesus and the chosen angels to observe these things without prejudgment and to do nothing out of favoritism.
Do not lay hands on anyone hastily, and do not share in sins that are not your own. Keep yourself pure.
Do not drink only water any longer, but drink a little wine because of your stomach and your frequent illnesses.
Some people's sins are obvious, going ahead of them to judgment, while for others they follow behind them.
Likewise, good deeds are also obvious, and those that are otherwise cannot remain hidden.
Let those who are under the yoke of slavery give their masters every honor, so that God's name and the teaching will not be slandered.

Those who have believing masters must not despise them because they are brothers. Instead, let them serve all the more, because those who benefit from their good work are believers and beloved. Teach these things and urge people to follow them.
But whoever teaches something different and does not accept the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and the teaching of godliness
is arrogant and understands nothing, but has an unhealthy obsession with questions and disputes. These give rise to envy, strife, slander, and evil thoughts,
deeds of people whose minds are corrupt and who have been deprived of the truth, thinking that serving God is a means of gain.
But godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we brought nothing into the world, and we cannot take anything out either.
But if we have food and clothing, these are enough for us.
But those who want to become rich will fall into temptation and a trap and many foolish and harmful desires, which drown people in destruction and ruin.
For the love of money is the root of every evil. Some, through loving it, have wandered away from the faith and subjected themselves to many sorrows.
But you, man of God, flee from these things. Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, and gentleness.
Fight the good fight of faith. Take hold of eternal life, to which you were called and for which you made the good confession before many witnesses.
I charge you before God, who gives life to everything, and Christ Jesus, who testified to the good confession before Pontius Pilate,
to keep the commandment without stain and without being found at fault in anything until the appearing of our Lord Jesus Christ,
which the blessed and only ruler will reveal at his appointed times, the King of kings and Lord of lords.
He alone has immortality and lives in light that no one can approach. No human being has seen him or can see him. To him belong honor and power forever and ever. Amen.
Command those who are rich in this present age not to be arrogant or put their hope in their wealth, which is uncertain, but in God, who richly gives us everything to enjoy.
Tell them to do good, to be rich in good deeds, to be generous and willing to share.
In this way they will store up for themselves a good foundation for the future, so that they may take hold of true life.
O Timothy, guard what has been entrusted to you, avoiding empty and profane talk and the opposing claims of falsely named knowledge.
Some have professed this knowledge and have strayed from the faith.
